summary: This bill amends the Truth in Lending Act to cap credit card interest rates at 10 percent including all finance charges, ban evasion via fees, allow consumers to recover excess payments within two years, impose penalties on violators, and automatically expire the cap on January 1, 2031.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Truth in Lending Act to impose a 10% cap on credit card interest rates, with enforcement mechanisms and a sunset provision. It does not authorize, appropriate, or reference any government spending, budget increases, or cuts. There is no fiscal expenditure involved; it is purely regulatory. No bearing on government spending levels.

The bill regulates credit card interest rates (finance charges), not taxes. It does not mention tax rates, tax policy, deductions, or revenue to government. Interest caps are distinct from taxation. No relation.
The bill concerns credit card lending practices and has no provisions related to healthcare coverage, providers, insurance, or public health systems. No bearing.
No mention of firearms, Second Amendment, regulations, or rights. Unrelated.
No provisions on immigration status, borders, pathways, or enforcement. Unrelated.
No reference to abortion access, restrictions, or related rights. Unrelated.
No impact on military funding, defense spending, or related policies. Unrelated.
No environmental protections, regulations, or climate measures. Unrelated.

While lower interest rates may indirectly help consumers avoid debt, the bill does not expand welfare programs, food stamps, unemployment benefits, or similar safety net entitlements. It is consumer financial regulation under the Truth in Lending Act, not social welfare policy. No direct engagement.
No provisions on schools, funding, choice, or federal involvement in education. Unrelated.
No relation to drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement. Unrelated.

Violations trigger civil penalties under section 130 of the Truth in Lending Act (forfeiture, recovery actions), not criminal sanctions, sentencing, policing, or justice reform. Does not engage criminal justice system.
No tariffs, trade agreements, protectionism, or globalization measures. Unrelated to international trade.
No discussion of deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy impacts. Regulatory change without budgetary effects specified. No bearing.
No provisions affecting LGBTQ+ protections or limitations. Unrelated.
No foreign assistance or aid programs mentioned. Unrelated.
No election reforms, voter access, or integrity measures. Unrelated.
Focuses on interest rates and fees for credit cards, not data privacy, tech oversight, or surveillance. No engagement with tech or privacy issues.
No worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility provisions. Unrelated to labor market.
No religious exemptions, civil rights, or discrimination issues. Unrelated.
